items.title: Prayer of Invocation & The Lord’s Prayer
items.text: Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy Name. Thy Kingdom come, thy will be done on earth, as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread, and forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors. Lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. For thine is the kingdom, the power, and the glory, forever. Amen.

lines.text: For behold, I create new heavens and a new earth,
and the former things shall not be remembered or come into mind.
But be glad and rejoice forever in that which I create;
for behold, I create Jerusalem to be a joy, and her people to be a gladness.
I will rejoice in Jerusalem and be glad in my people;
no more shall be heard in it the sound of weeping and the cry of distress.
No more shall there be in it an infant who lives but a few days,
or an old man who does not fill out his days,
The wolf and the lamb shall graze together; the lion shall eat straw like the ox, and dust shall be the serpent’s food.
They shall not hurt or destroy in all my holy mountain,” says the Lord.

items.title: Corporate Prayer of Confession
items.text: Merciful God, always with us, always coming: We confess that we do not know how to prepare for your Advent. We have forgotten how to hope in miracles; we have ignored the promise of your kingdom; we get distracted by all the busyness of this season. Forgive us, God. Grant us the simple wonder of the shepherds, the intelligent courage of the Magi, and the patient faith of Mary and Joseph, that we may journey with them to Bethlehem and find the good news of a child born for us. Now, in the quiet of our hearts, we ask you to make us ready for his coming.

notes.label: The Advent Wreath
notes.text: As we light the Advent candles, we remember God’s covenant faithfulness. Just as Israel watched in darkness for the promised Messiah, the Church today watches in hope for Christ’s return. The growing light reminds us that Jesus Christ, the Light of the World, has come to dispel the darkness of sin and will come again to make all things new.

notes.label: The Lord’s Prayer
notes.text: In the Reformed faith, we recognize that the whole Word of God is of use to direct us in prayer, yet Christ gave us this specific prayer as a special rule and pattern. From its opening address to its closing doxology, the Lord’s Prayer teaches us to approach God with reverence and confidence, prioritizing his kingdom and glory while trusting him for our daily bread, pardon, and protection.

notes.label: O Come, O Come, Emmanuel
notes.text: Rooted in the ancient O Antiphons, this hymn frames Advent through God’s covenantal faithfulness and sovereign providence. Drawing on Israel’s exile and Old Testament Messianic titles, it confesses that salvation rests entirely on God’s initiative to rescue His people from bondage. We sing it not in uncertain longing, but in assured hope: the covenant-keeping God who sovereignly fulfilled His promises in Christ’s first coming will just as certainly consummate His kingdom at His return.

sermon.title: Greater Glory: I Am With You
intro: We are kicking off the Advent season today with a series that’s going to take us through the OT prophecy of a guy named Haggai. Our sermon series for Advent is called “Greater Glory” and will invite us to pause and consider this period of time when we are waiting for Jesus to return and establish his glory in the new Jerusalem.

This series will take us through the book of Haggai and highlight four promises that God makes to God’s covenant people, promises that are ultimately found and fulfilled in the arrival of Jesus. Jesus, the “Treasure of All Nations” (Haggai 2:7), comes to show the world a greater vision for our lives, and God’s Spirit guides our hearts and hands to wait with purpose and work with hope.

Advent is about more than remembering that Jesus came into the world. It’s about remembering that our deepest hope is found in the God who comes to dwell with His people. The people in Haggai’s day needed more than a building project. They needed the presence of God. So do we!
